## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d6f79bbd8a49a5a916fe0642bdbdd227bd4ac383`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/triage-duties.md + scripts/pm/first-touch-sweep.mjs, scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs

PR #35373, card #35234. Read: the card body and all seven comments, the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` (3 files), the check-runs on this head, and the cited rule files in the PR tree (read, not reviewed).

### ① Derived judgments

- Sweep ① accept-set: a card carrying only a `domain:*` (no `pm:*`, no `needs-user-decision`, no `area:*`) is now listed; a card carrying only an `area:*` leaves ① and is ③ once settled. Right: it is the rule line as rewritten, and `classify()` reads it the same way.
- Sweep ②: `pm:queue` with a `domain:*` and no `area:*` is now listed on the multi-lane board; `pm:queue` + `area:*` with no `domain:*` leaves ②. Right.
- Sweep ③ and ④: the population moves from `domain:*` carriers to `area:*` carriers; the state set (`PM_EXCLUSIVE_STATE_LABELS`) and the settle window are unchanged. Right.
- H13: same swap; `PM_STATE_LABELS`, `H13_EXEMPT_LABELS`, the 2h threshold and the P0-suspect line are unchanged. A `domain:*`-only aged card leaves H13 and is the sweep's ①. Right, and stated in the header and pinned by two self-test cases.
- Exported names: `h13DomainWithoutPmState` becomes `h13AreaWithoutPmState`, `DOMAIN_HALF_STATE_STALE_HOURS` becomes `AREA_HALF_STATE_STALE_HOURS`. No reader of the old names is left in the PR tree (searched). Right.
- Sweep output: `--json` gains `no_type` (additive); the text gains one backstop row and the existing row's label changes from `area backstop` to `area:* backstop`. No program in the tree parses that line. Right.
- New accept-set, `lacksType()`: open cards with an empty REST `type`, minus the sweep's exclusions, `security` and `pm:epic`. The two extra exemptions are WRONG as derived from the rule text: see S1.
- Verdict and exit code: the two backstop rows stay outside `owed`, the verdict and the exit. Right. Note the overlap the self-test itself names: a queued card with no `area:*` is on the backstop row and is also a ② debt.
- Gate verdicts on this head: every check-run is `success` or `skipped`, including `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. All 59 check-runs finished: 33 `success`, 26 `skipped`, none failed (`Test Core` and `Live half-state sweep` included).

### ② Semver level

No changeset, label `skip-changeset`, and `Check Changeset` is green. Right: the diff touches `scripts/pm/**` and one `.claude/**` reference file; no package, no published schema.

Clause-②: no — holds. Nothing a consumer of a published package can observe changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (keep `Fixes` or switch to `Part of`): answered on the head. The PR body says `Part of #35234`, and the Part-of guard is green. That agrees with the card: its Done-when (no script under `scripts/pm/` needs a `domain:*` label) does not hold while other readings of a card's `domain:*` remain (seen in the tree: H74's inheritance test in `check-half-states.mjs`, a second per-card `domain:` filter there, and the seat-row match in `fleet-roster.mjs`; the PR body's full list of six was not re-derived). The card stays open and carries them.
- Dev flag `check:platform-checklist` red on base and head: none of this PR's three paths is involved; not judged here.
- Dev flags with `carrier: none` (the stale `ensure-pm-labels.sh` comment; `SKILL.md` lane table): see N3. The open card carries the six readings; these two text leftovers have no named carrier yet. For the seat to route, not a blocker on this head.
- Dev report says the PR body carries six 维护者速读 lines; the body carries four. Body shape is the body guards' question (green), not ④'s.
- Label retirement: not done here, listed for the maintainer in the PR body, as the card and the claim require.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No query, no id materialisation, no in-app join; the scripts read the REST issue list they already read.

### ④ Design judgment

`triage-duties.md` (hits). The three changed lines hold against `first-touch-sweep.mjs`: each of the four rewritten disjunction phrases and the backstop phrase is a verbatim member of `TRIAGE_RULE_PHRASES` / `AREA_BACKSTOP_PHRASE`, the self-test reads them from the file, and the file stays at 108 lines. Against the neighbouring rule text it also holds: `filing-gate.md` has the filing seat or triage's first touch write `area:*` and the issue type on every public card, so `area:*` is the label a first touch leaves, and `seat-lifecycle.md` puts `tracking` on an epic parent, which the exclusions already drop. Tried to break it with cloud cards (`domain:cloud` cards carry a live state and `area:cloud`, so they are not ①), with epic parents (excluded by `tracking`) and with `finding` cards (③ treats them as before the swap). None breaks.

`first-touch-sweep.mjs` (implementing). `classify()` agrees with lines ①–④ sentence by sentence. `lacksArea()` agrees with `SKILL.md` (a security card in this repo takes no area).

S1 (should-fix) — `lacksType()` exempts `pm:epic` and `security`, and no rule grants either. The rule line in this same PR says the daily read scans public cards with no `area:*` or no type, with no exception. The jsdoc says "an epic takes no type by rule"; no such sentence exists in `SKILL.md`, `filing-gate.md`, `triage-duties.md`, `seat-lifecycle.md` or `lanes/triage.md` in the PR tree. What the tree does say: `pm:epic` sits on a parent OR a sub-issue (`SKILL.md` label table); a sub-issue is an ordinary work card, and `filing-gate.md` refuses a fleet card filed without a type; the epic parent is already dropped by `tracking`. So the exemption only hides typeless work cards that happen to carry `pm:epic`, and a self-test case pins that hiding as intended. For `security`, the rule excuses the AREA only. Fix one way or the other: drop the two exemptions from the type row (and the two cases that pin them), or put the exemption in the rule text with its source and keep the code. Report-only row, outside the verdict, so not a must-fix.

`check-half-states.mjs` (implementing, H13 only). `h13AreaWithoutPmState()` agrees with the header, with rule line ③ and with the finding text; the four new cases cover both directions of the swap. No finding.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1 — `triage-duties.md` backstop line: the old sentence ended in 补齐 (scan and fill in); the new one says only 扫 (scan). The duty to fill in is now implied by the first half of the line. Prose; fix if the line budget allows, else accepted.
- N2 — `first-touch-sweep.mjs`: the classifier battery registers 19 cases and its floor is pinned at 18, so one case can be deleted without a red. The H13 fixture builder is still named `domainCard`. Leave as accepted deviations or a follow-up; a fix here moves the head.
- N3 — text that now disagrees with the two script headers ("a `domain:*` label routes nothing"), all OUTSIDE this diff and not reviewed: `SKILL.md` still says `domain:*` decides file ownership and is written in the first touch; `ensure-pm-labels.sh` still describes ③ and H13 as reading `domain:*`. Also inside the diff, the backstop jsdoc still gives "a board mid-backfill must not turn every sweep into FOUND" as its reason, while ①/② now do count a queued card with no `area:*`. Belongs to the lane-to-seat text step; name a carrier.

S1 is open on this head. No must-fix.

- `check-half-states.mjs`: a rename of one self-test helper (`domainCard` to `labelledCard`) and one comment. No function, constant, finding text or case changes. Right.
- Gate verdicts on this head: all 54 check-runs finished, 32 `success` and 22 `skipped`, none failed. Green ones include `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Test Core`, `Live half-state sweep`, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from round 1: no changeset, `skip-changeset`; the delta touches only `scripts/pm/**` and one `.claude/**` reference file.

Clause-②: no — holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No new dev flag or open question in this delta.
- Round 1's answers stand: the PR is `Part of #35234`, the card stays open for the remaining `domain:*` readings, the label retirement is the maintainer's later step.
- SQL push-down: not applicable; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed. `lacksType()` now drops only the sweep's exclusions; the `security` and `pm:epic` exemptions are gone, the jsdoc no longer cites a rule that does not exist, and the header says the `security` exemption is the area row's alone. The two cases that pinned the hiding are removed, and the walk case now requires the typeless security card on the row in both `noType` and `--json`, and in the rendered line.

The backstop battery floor moving 16 to 14 is honest. The battery had 16 cases; exactly the two exemption cases were removed and none added; the battery registers 14 on this head (counted in the tree), so the floor equals the registered count as it did before. It is not a loosened guard: the coverage those two cases gave was of behaviour that no longer exists, and the opposite behaviour is now asserted by the walk case.

`triage-duties.md` (hits). The backstop line again ends in 补齐, so the duty to fill in is stated; the line still names both `area:*` and type; the file is still 108 lines. It agrees with `lacksArea()` / `lacksType()` and with `filing-gate.md` (every public card owes an area and a type).

N1: closed (补齐 restored).
N2: half closed. The helper is renamed. The classifier battery still registers 19 cases against a floor of 18; accepted deviation, no effect on correctness.
N3: the in-diff part is closed: the backstop jsdoc now says a listed card that is bare or queued with no `area:*` is owed through ① or ② already, and the rows add no debt of their own. The out-of-diff part (`SKILL.md` and `ensure-pm-labels.sh` wording on `domain:*`) is unchanged, not reviewed, and still needs a named carrier in the lane-to-seat text step.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
